notes: Business Analyst / SRS authoring skill (SDLC Stage 2, REQUIREMENT checkpoint). Evaluate by checking it detects project context, extracts actors + Given-When-Then user stories + testable acceptance criteria + edge cases, and writes docs/streams/[feature]-[YYYYMMDD]/requirements/SRS.md; positives should fire, the design boundary should route to design-function.

evals.prompt: Analyze the requirements for the user management module and write the SRS.
evals.expected_output: Reads CLAUDE.md/PROJECT.md for context, then produces docs/streams/user-management-[YYYYMMDD]/requirements/SRS.md: actors/roles, Given-When-Then user stories, testable acceptance criteria (1:1 with test cases), business rules, and edge cases (empty state, error, permission denied, soft delete). Stops at REQUIREMENT without doing technical design.

evals.prompt: Define the user stories and acceptance criteria for the payment feature so QA can write test cases from them.
evals.expected_output: Extracts user stories in Given-When-Then form and acceptance criteria that are each writable as a test case, maps to any existing API/screen docs, flags dependencies and risks, and writes docs/streams/payment-[YYYYMMDD]/requirements/SRS.md. Does not implement or design endpoints.

evals.prompt: Design the ORM schema and API endpoints for the user management module.
evals.expected_output: Should route to design-function / not fire, because this asks for technical/API + ORM design (TECH spec), not requirement analysis or an SRS artifact.
